why: The route pages and glacier article I could read give no description of how the scramble line meets the Flett Glacier.
An American Alpine Club report and a Mountain Project route page describe the way to the col as snow, slab and talus in Crescent Creek Basin and a snow gully, with the glacier only on the far side.
The Mountain Project route page gives no approach and no mention of glacier or snow, so the line's relation to the Terror Glacier stays open.
A park ranger conditions report from mid-August describes the Pyramid route as rock scrambling mixed with firm snow.
Wikipedia gives only that snow can lie on the peak in late spring and early fall, with no route detail.
No page I could read describes this ridge traverse's snow in July to September.
Wikipedia puts the Fairchild Glacier on the northeast side and calls the easiest route a class 3 scramble, but does not say the line avoids the ice.

A Mountain Project route page describes the approach descending steep snow from Burgundy Col onto the Silver Star Glacier and recommends glacier gear, and the route text itself says it is reached via that glacier.
The Mountain Project area page for Pernod Spire describes only the west face approach and says nothing of snow on the south face.
The only page found was Wikipedia, which lists no route or snow detail.
No route or snow page for this peak turned up.

Mountain Project route and area pages and a park conditions report describe the Goodell Creek, Stump Hollow and Barrier approach to a rock ridge, with no glacier travel reported for the Chopping Block.

Held at unsure on review: no page specific to this route was read; it rests on the shared approach. The same Mountain Project area page and park conditions report describe the shared Stump Hollow and Barrier approach to rock ledges, with no glacier travel reported.

Held at unsure on review: a single first-ascent account, and a glacier is named as an alternative way in. An American Alpine Club first-ascent report describes a brush-and-river approach to the Mox basin and a rappel descent of the face, naming a glacier only as a rejected alternative on the far side.
The Mountain Project area page lists no routes and gives no snow detail for the standard scramble.
No page on this route was found.
An old American Alpine Club account crossed a heavily crevassed glacier to the face, but the current Mountain Project page uses a ledge approach with no glacier mentioned.
Wikipedia lists only a scramble via the south ridge and no snow detail for the route.
The Mountain Project page tags the route as snow but gives no season or conditions.
Traverse accounts from the American Alpine Club describe the rock but not the snow or glacier on the approach to this notch.
No page on this route was reached; peakbagger returned 403.
